title: Track repository assessment follow-ups
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

The assessment found a working compiler/runtime pipeline and strong behavioral coverage, alongside three reproducible defects and broader architectural, documentation, and performance gaps. Track the findings together while distinguishing immediate fixes from lower-priority framework enhancements.

Validation baseline: package build, workspace type checks, formatting, lint (with warnings), 191 Rust tests, 520 runtime executions, 180 compiled browser-corpus executions, tooling/addon/example tests, docs production build, 19 size fixtures, and the existing compiler benchmark passed. Browser totals include engine repetitions. Counter gzip: 8,004 bytes; TodoMVC gzip: 11,778 bytes. Packed-consumer installation and the release platform matrix were not executed.

Lower-priority layout retention and streaming are documented product limitations, not regressions or prerequisites for fixing the confirmed bugs.

## Success Criteria
- Each confirmed defect is fixed with regression coverage.
- Architectural and compatibility claims are reconciled with executable evidence.
- Performance validation exercises source edits and larger updater graphs.
- Lower-priority scope is completed or explicitly dispositioned with a recorded rationale.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each confirmed defect is fixed with regression coverage.
- Architectural and compatibility claims are reconciled with executable evidence.
- Performance validation exercises source edits and larger updater graphs.
- Lower-priority scope is completed or explicitly dispositioned with a recorded rationale.

title: Bound the Vite compilation cache across source edits
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

The compilation cache is keyed by source content/configuration and retains generated code, source maps, and analysis indefinitely. Hot-update invalidation clears dependency helpers but does not evict obsolete compilation entries.

Evidence: packages/vite-plugin/src/index.ts:60,87,130,340,377.

## Steps to Reproduce
Create one vidact() plugin instance. Transform tests/runtime-size/fixtures/counter.tsx 30 times with a distinct appended comment for each edit, using the same filename and environment. Invoke handleHotUpdate({file: filename}) after each transform. Instrumenting the compilation Map showed 30 retained entries for one file.

Long development sessions retain obsolete compilations. Prefer a bounded cache or replacement by module/environment/target/configuration while preserving correctness across dependency capsule changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Repeated edits to a fixed set of modules retain a bounded number of compilation records.
- Unchanged inputs still benefit from caching.
- Target, feature, environment, and dependency invalidation behavior remains correct.
- A regression test exercises many source revisions and verifies eviction or replacement.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repeated edits to a fixed set of modules retain a bounded number of compilation records.
- Unchanged inputs still benefit from caching.
- Target, feature, environment, and dependency invalidation behavior remains correct.
- A regression test exercises many source revisions and verifies eviction or replacement.
close_reason: Bound the compilation cache per module configuration and added revision replacement coverage.

title: Support incremental document streaming in the Start handler
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

Although the runtime exposes renderToReadableStream, createStartHandler buffers it with await new Response(stream).text() before building the final document. Start therefore does not currently deliver incremental application HTML through this path.

Evidence: packages/start/src/server.ts:113-129; docs/architecture/vidact-start-file-route-lifecycle.md.

This is a documented framework limitation. Design a streaming document API and its interaction with snapshots, custom renderDocument callbacks, and hydration markers before changing the public handler contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Record a streaming document and snapshot protocol with explicit custom-document compatibility.
- The response delivers an initial document chunk before a delayed async boundary settles.
- Later chunks preserve runtime ownership markers and hydration correctness.
- Abort, error, HEAD, and navigation-snapshot paths are covered.
- Add an integration test using a controlled delayed boundary and a streaming reader.
- Update Start documentation to describe the actual streaming guarantees.
acceptance_criteria:
- Record a streaming document and snapshot protocol with explicit custom-document compatibility.
- The response delivers an initial document chunk before a delayed async boundary settles.
- Later chunks preserve runtime ownership markers and hydration correctness.
- Abort, error, HEAD, and navigation-snapshot paths are covered.
- Add an integration test using a controlled delayed boundary and a streaming reader.
- Update Start documentation to describe the actual streaming guarantees.

title: Declare Start HTML and navigation response variation
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

Start serves HTML and navigation JSON at the same URL based on x-vidact-start-navigation, but neither successful response declares Vary. A cache that stores these responses can reuse the wrong representation.

Evidence: packages/start/src/server.ts:94-130; packages/start/src/snapshot.ts.

## Steps to Reproduce
Create a Start manifest with one component and loader. Request the same URL once without the navigation header and once with x-vidact-start-navigation: 1. The actual handler returned text/html and application/x-vidact-start+json respectively; both responses contained only a content-type header.

This reproduction establishes missing response metadata, not a demonstrated issue on a particular deployed CDN.

## Acceptance Criteria
- HTML and snapshot responses declare Vary: x-vidact-start-navigation.
- Existing Vary values are preserved where response customization applies.
- GET and HEAD behavior is covered.
- Document the caching policy and verify a Vary-aware cache distinguishes the two representations.
acceptance_criteria:
- HTML and snapshot responses declare Vary: x-vidact-start-navigation.
- Existing Vary values are preserved where response customization applies.
- GET and HEAD behavior is covered.
- Document the caching policy and verify a Vary-aware cache distinguishes the two representations.

title: Preserve destination fragments during Start client navigation
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

The server snapshot contains pathname and search only. performNavigation reconstructs nextUrl from that snapshot, losing the requested target.hash before history update and scrolling.

Evidence: packages/start/src/client.ts:124-141; packages/start/src/server.ts:97.

## Steps to Reproduce
From /, navigate to /page#section with a successful /page snapshot response. Running the actual client navigation code with mocked rendering returned true, pushed https://example.test/page, and invoked scrollTo({top:0,left:0,behavior:'instant'}) instead of scrolling to section.

Preserve requested fragments through navigation, with an explicit policy for redirected destinations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Cross-route navigation to an existing fragment preserves the hash and scrolls to that element.
- scroll:false preserves the destination URL without scrolling.
- replace navigation, missing fragments, and redirect interactions are covered.
- Existing native same-page hash-link behavior is preserved.
- Add browser-level regression coverage for the successful cross-route path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cross-route navigation to an existing fragment preserves the hash and scrolls to that element.
- scroll:false preserves the destination URL without scrolling.
- replace navigation, missing fragments, and redirect interactions are covered.
- Existing native same-page hash-link behavior is preserved.
- Add browser-level regression coverage for the successful cross-route path.

title: Reconcile runtime updater ordering with the compiler-owned scheduling contract
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

The README and architecture describe compiler-owned ordering and no browser dependency discovery. createScope calls topologicalUpdaterOrder on first flush and after updater registration/removal. That function constructs pairwise read/write edges and computes strongly connected components in the browser. The order is cached; this is not read-time dependency tracking or a demonstrated rendering bug.

Evidence: packages/runtime/src/compiled/core.ts:941,951,1090; crates/vidact-compiler/src/ir.rs; README.md:173; docs/architecture/react-analysis-boundary.md.

Evaluate whether compiler-emitted order can cover runtime memo and dynamically registered updater cases. If runtime ordering remains required, state the precise boundary and its scaling implications rather than removing correctness safeguards solely to match prose.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Record the supported ordering contract and the reason for any runtime ordering in docs/architecture.
- Align README and IR documentation with actual behavior.
- Benchmark increasing updater counts and registration/removal churn.
- Preserve memo prerequisite ordering, cycles/stabilization behavior, and existing browser semantics.
- Implement any selected optimization with regression and size-budget evidence, or record why it is deferred.

- Record the supported ordering contract and the reason for any runtime ordering in docs/architecture.
- Align README and IR documentation with actual behavior.

title: Refresh React compatibility claims and stale architecture evidence
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

README.md:52 claims most React components compile without changes; line 177 broadly describes Base UI/shadcn dependency support. Existing tests establish specific supported behaviors rather than a measured general compatibility rate.

The architecture record docs/architecture/shadcn-base-ui-compatibility-corpus.md refers to files no longer present, including examples/docs/src/shadcn-compatibility.ts and examples/docs/scripts/audit-shadcn-compatibility.mjs, plus removed browser proofs. Historical counts in that record must not be treated as current certification.

Current evidence includes packages/vite-plugin/test/base-ui.integration.test.ts, tests/browser/corpus/apps/base-ui-dependency, examples/docs/src/DocsShell.browser.test.ts, and docs/react-compatibility.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replace broad unsupported claims with a precise, evidence-backed compatibility description.
- Distinguish compile, SSR, browser interaction, DOM ownership, and typing guarantees.
- Repair stale evidence paths or mark historical records superseded with links to current contracts.
- Every claimed certified surface points to a current executable test.
- Add a practical check or maintenance convention for keeping compatibility evidence current.

title: Benchmark changed-source compilation and larger updater graphs
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

scripts/benchmark.mjs:22-49 repeatedly transforms unchanged fixture text using one plugin instance. Its incremental timing mainly measures cache hits, and its heap-retention loop does not exercise edit-history growth. The runtime budget test uses 100 mounts and 20 updates of a single-state fixture with a broad five-second ceiling.

Evidence: scripts/benchmark.mjs; packages/runtime/test/performance/runtime-budgets.browser.test.ts; tests/runtime-size/measure.mjs.

Keep the useful cache-hit and bundle checks while adding representative changed-source and scaling workloads. Avoid asserting comparative framework performance from these smoke budgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Report cold compilation, unchanged-cache hits, and changed-source transforms separately.
- Exercise many revisions of the same modules and verify bounded retained compilation data after warmup.
- Include larger updater graphs, keyed-list changes, and registration/disposal churn.
- Record fixture sizes, runtime environment, sampling method, and justified regression thresholds.
- Preserve deterministic correctness and size checks alongside timing measurements.

title: Plan cohesive boundaries for the compiler and runtime core
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

crates/vidact-compiler/src/surgical_codegen/mod.rs is approximately 6,001 lines and packages/runtime/src/compiled/core.ts approximately 4,041 lines at the assessed checkout. Their concentration of interacting concerns makes changes harder to reason about; size alone does not establish a defect.

Identify boundaries around responsibilities such as scheduling, ownership/publication, and codegen lowering that reduce coupling without introducing a generic framework or broad rewrite. This task produces a concrete incremental plan; it does not authorize an arbitrary large refactor.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Map the major responsibilities, shared state, and invariants in both files.
- Select one or two cohesive extraction candidates and explain their practical benefit.
- Specify how ownership, transaction behavior, ABI, and bundle size will be preserved.
- Link existing tests that guard each candidate and identify any missing behavioral proof.
- Record an incremental implementation plan or a reason to leave a boundary intact.

title: Expand browser-certified published React dependency coverage
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

Published dependency compilation and SSR tests are valuable but do not establish browser interactions and ownership guarantees for the entire imported package. Current Base UI browser coverage proves a specific Button/renderable path; the removed historical shadcn corpus should not stand in for active tests.

Use packages/vite-plugin/test/base-ui.integration.test.ts and tests/browser/corpus/apps/base-ui-dependency as starting evidence. Audit existing proofs before adding tests, then select a small set of already-compiling published component paths with useful interaction coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Maintain a current inventory separating production compilation, SSR, browser interaction, ownership, and type coverage.
- Add compiled TSX browser proofs for selected uncovered published dependency paths.
- Assert interaction results, retained DOM identity, bounded mutations, and disposal cleanup.
- Exercise client and hydration behavior where claimed across the configured browser engines.
- Unsupported constructs retain explicit diagnostics; local replacements are labeled separately from upstream-library support.

title: Retain unchanged Start layout owners during navigation
description:
Source: repository assessment on 2026-09-05, checkout f049ca9. Findings were reviewed locally; this issue tracks follow-up work, not a completed fix.

Start currently replaces the entire owned route root on successful navigation, resetting component-local state in shared layouts. This is explicitly documented in packages/start/README.md:63 and docs/architecture/vidact-start-file-route-lifecycle.md, so treat it as a future lifecycle feature rather than a regression.

Evidence: packages/start/src/client.ts:139; packages/runtime/src/root.ts.

Define which matched layouts retain identity when route params, loader data, or child routes change before implementing retention.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Record the layout identity and loader/prop update contract.
- Navigating between siblings preserves unchanged layout state and DOM owners.
- Changed layouts dispose exactly once and publish replacement ownership safely.
- Cancellation, failed navigation, back/forward, hydration, and updated loader data are covered.
- Browser tests prove retained identity and bounded mutations.
- Update the documented navigation limitations after implementation.

- Navigating between siblings preserves unchanged layout state and DOM owners.
